Public Utility Commission of Texas

Austin, TX 78711-3326

Dear Chairman Gteeson, I am pleading with you to intervene in the 7651<V Transmission
Line project, Big Hill Bell Count East (PUC Docket 59475) tothe Perian Basin from here in
Central Texas. l stronglyoppose this project due to its significant and devastating impact
on families, their property, their homes, and lives here in ourcommunities.

The people in ourcommunities, especiallythose living nearthe proposed [jnes, are
concerned with the long-term health effects of the Electro Magnetic Fields. We have folks
with small children, and people that are cancer-risk, and those with pacemakers, etc. The
lawyers representing ONCOR and LCRA will be quicl<to dismiss these concerns as
"unproven". However, there plenty of studiesthatwould indicate otherwise. Woutd they
live beside these lines if they had a choice?

The people are faced with property devaluation, financial harm, restrictions on land use,
and agricultural harm. Theyare faced with paying propertytaxes on land they can't use.
Many are now facing being uprooted from their long-time homes, and newlyconstructed
homes because they can't and won't live beside these lines. These lines and their
monstrous infrastructure will decimate neighborhoods and rural communities with
extensive land clearing leading to destruction of wildlife habitat, loss of vegetation, and
long-term ecological disruption.

There is no fairness, in this case, for landowners and homeowners. The majority, who
received notices just weeks ago, a few we know only days ago, either do not have the
resources, or did not have time to secure legal representation to effectively participate in
these regulatory proceedings that can be quite complex.

Oncorand LCRA are proposingthesetransmission lines tearacrossthe most beautiful
areas in the state. The planned routes forthe hideous towers and lines, comparable in size
to the Statue of Liberty, are traversing our properties, splitting our properties in two,
drastically devaluing our properties, our homes, and devastating our lives.
 l ask you to help by delaying this process to allow time to consider alternative ways to meet
energy demands. The HB 5066 calls for consideration of a range of solutions to meet
growingenergydemands. Whydoes it have to be this? Why in such a hurry? There must
be time allowed to consider other solutions that reduce the harmful impact on private
lands and property owners. I urge you to consider a way forward that is fair for landowners,
and homeowners, that ensures their property rights and fairness and quality of life through
this process. Thankyou for yourconsideration in this matter.

                                           Sincerely,
